title: A Survey of Audio-Visual Collaboration for Embodied Intelligence
description: A unified capability-oriented survey of how visual and auditory evidence supports embodied perception, reasoning, and interaction in a closed loop.

affiliations.name: State Key Laboratory of Networking and Switching Technology, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing, China
School of Computer Science, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing, China
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), Guangzhou, China

abstract: Audio-visual embodied intelligence (AVEI) studies how complementary visual and auditory observations support agents' understanding and interaction with their environments. Vision captures appearance, geometry, and motion, while sound provides cues about off-screen events, physical interactions, and spoken intent. This survey organizes the field through a unified Perception–Reasoning–Interaction taxonomy based on principal outputs and functional roles. Perception covers cross-modal consistency, grounding, analysis, and scene understanding; Reasoning examines specialized models, foundation models, and agentic systems; Interaction encompasses mobility, manipulation, communication, and generalist policies.

Rather than assuming a strict progression between these capabilities, we examine their functional connections within a closed loop: perception supplies evidence, reasoning guides decisions, and interaction produces feedback for subsequent understanding. We synthesize methodological developments, consolidate datasets, simulators, and benchmarks, and identify shared challenges in evidence grounding, streaming fusion, memory, acoustic transfer, and closed-loop evaluation. Throughout, we emphasize when auditory information changes an agent's decisions and whether those changes improve embodied performance.
